ideas.title: How to reserve and collect evening loaves — Vale Street Bakery's 4-week trial (starts 24 Nov)
ideas.description: A concise how-to for regular customers explaining how to reserve a loaf by telephone before noon on Tuesdays and Thursdays and collect it from 17:30–18:30 at the side door; sets expectations about the trial (reserved loaves come from that day's normal bake; no extra evening batch) and the unchanged Saturday counter hours.
ideas.audience: Regular customers of Vale Street Bakery
ideas.rationale: The update itself says its useful job is to make the new collection choice easy to understand for existing customers; a short practical guide will make the reservation/collection steps and limits explicit during the four-week trial.
ideas.evidence: During two informal evenings in October, staff handed over 14 and 11 reserved loaves. Three loaves were left uncollected on the second evening and were donated with the ordinary surplus the next morning.

ideas.title: What the early trial numbers show — facts and limits
ideas.description: A short item that presents the October handover counts (14 and 11), notes three uncollected loaves were donated, makes clear those counts excluded counter shoppers, and highlights that the baker has not calculated waste or revenue changes and that a four-week review is planned with no extension commitment.
ideas.audience: Local readers and regular customers interested in the pilot's early operational data
ideas.rationale: Readers will get clear value from seeing the available empirical counts and the explicit gaps in measurement (exclusions and no waste/revenue calculation) so they understand what the numbers can and cannot imply.
ideas.evidence: During two informal evenings in October, staff handed over 14 and 11 reserved loaves. Three loaves were left uncollected on the second evening and were donated with the ordinary surplus the next morning. These counts do not include shoppers who used the counter and were not compared with earlier weeks. The baker has not calculated waste or revenue changes. A review of the trial is planned after four weeks, with no commitment yet to extend it.

grounding.claim: The bakery is running a four-week evening collection trial starting 24 November.
grounding.sourceEvidence: a four-week evening collection trial starting 24 November.
grounding.inference: The quoted phrase directly names the trial's duration (four weeks) and its start date (24 November), which supports including those specifics in the title.
grounding.constraints: The source gives start date and duration but no calendar end date beyond 'four weeks'; it does not describe any exceptions to the trial period.

grounding.claim: Customers can reserve a loaf by telephone before noon on Tuesdays and Thursdays and collect it from 17:30 to 18:30 at the side door.
grounding.sourceEvidence: On Tuesdays and Thursdays, customers can reserve a loaf by telephone before noon and collect it from 17:30 to 18:30 at the side door.
grounding.inference: The sentence specifies the reservation method, time cutoff, days, collection window and collection location, which supports describing the practical reservation/collection steps in the how-to.
grounding.constraints: The quote specifies those days and times but does not list exceptions, accessibility details, or how many loaves may be reserved per call.

grounding.claim: The update is intended for regular customers of Vale Street Bakery.
grounding.sourceEvidence: An update for regular customers of Vale Street Bakery introduces a four-week evening collection trial starting 24 November.
grounding.inference: The source explicitly identifies the message as 'An update for regular customers', which supports naming regular customers as the primary audience.
grounding.constraints: While addressed to regular customers, the information will also be visible to others; the source does not define 'regular' or specify how it is distributed.

grounding.claim: The update's stated purpose is to make the new collection choice easy to understand for people who already buy there, so a practical guide is appropriate.
grounding.sourceEvidence: The update's useful job is to make the new collection choice easy to understand for people who already buy there.
grounding.inference: The sentence states the communicative purpose directly; that purpose implies a reader need for clarity about the new option, which justifies producing a concise practical guide.
grounding.constraints: The source states the intended communicative role but does not report whether customers found previous communications confusing or what specific questions they have.

grounding.claim: Informal October evenings handed over 14 and 11 reserved loaves; three uncollected loaves on the second evening were donated the next morning.
grounding.sourceEvidence: During two informal evenings in October, staff handed over 14 and 11 reserved loaves. Three loaves were left uncollected on the second evening and were donated with the ordinary surplus the next morning.
grounding.inference: Those two contiguous sentences report the observed counts and the donation of uncollected loaves, supporting the factual statement about early trial numbers and handling of uncollected items.
grounding.constraints: These counts are limited to two informal evenings in October and the source notes they 'do not include shoppers who used the counter' and were 'not compared with earlier weeks', so they cannot be taken as comprehensive evidence of typical demand.
